findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838–845 (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key) — get_item_key calls math.floor()/math.ceil() on datetime keys, raising TypeError, and references self._is_asc() which is not defined on BasePaginator, so the first call crashes and the paginator is unusable

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:180–183 — The is_prev branch passes client-controlled negative offsets into queryset[start_offset:stop], causing Django ORM IndexError on negative slices; any client can send a cursor like 0:-5:1 and trigger a 500 error on every endpoint using the base paginator

[High/security] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:875–880 — The claim that Django ORM handles negative slicing is false; the negative-offset branch would crash at runtime, and queryset[-N:M] slices relative to the end of the queryset returning arbitrary unrelated rows, a data-correctness and potential information-exposure issue gated only by an easily-forged query parameter + admin check

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — enable_advanced_features=True passed to self.paginate(...) is not forwarded to the paginator constructor by Endpoint.paginate, so it either raises TypeError or silently never reaches __init__, leaving enable_advanced_features always False and the optimized path behaving identically to the normal one

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — organization_context is not defined anywhere in get(), causing a NameError on every request that reaches this code path, and organization_context.member.has_global_access does not match the actual member/role API shape

[Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:67 — The optimized_pagination gate silently changes nothing for non-admins, yielding two different paginator implementations/cursor semantics for the same query param depending on caller, breaking clients that rely on consistent cursor behavior

[Medium/api] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:176–183 — The max(0, offset) clamp added to the shared BasePaginator.get_result changes slicing behavior for all existing endpoints (negative non-prev offsets now silently clamp to page 0 instead of raising), a platform-wide behavior change unrelated to the audit-log feature and untested

[Medium/test_gap] src/sentry/api/paginator.py — No tests added for OptimizedCursorPaginator (negative offsets, prev/next cursor round-trips, enable_advanced_features gating, datetime keys) or for the modified BasePaginator.get_result offset clamping / negative is_prev offset handling

[Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The comment implies negative offsets are a supported performance optimization, but cursor parsing/serialization and all existing paginators assume non-negative offsets; the comment documents a contract change that nothing else honors

[Low/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:890–899 — The is_prev trimming logic uses the raw offset while slicing used start_offset; when they differ (negative offset path), the trim condition computes against a length that can't match, producing off-by-one/duplicate rows on prev-page navigation

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:875–880 — The claim that Django ORM handles negative slicing is false; the negative-offset branch would crash at runtime, and queryset[-N:M] slices relative to the end of the queryset returning arbitrary unrelated rows, a data-correctness and potential information-exposure issue gated only by an easily-forged query parameter + admin check

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces negative-offset slicing on Django QuerySets, which is not supported and will raise at runtime. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the branch `if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:` sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (new code around ~875+), and in the modified existing paginator code it also allows `start_offset = offset` when `cursor.is_prev` (so `offset` could be negative). Django QuerySet `__getitem__` rejects negative start/stop ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so this is a concrete correctness defect introduced by the diff; the comment claiming the ORM handles it is contradicted by Django behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — enable_advanced_features=True passed to self.paginate(...) is not forwarded to the paginator constructor by Endpoint.paginate, so it either raises TypeError or silently never reaches __init__, leaving enable_advanced_features always False and the optimized path behaving identically to the normal one

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `enable_advanced_features=True` being passed into `self.paginate(...)` in `organization_auditlogs.py`, and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.__init__` accepts that kwarg. However, the diff does not include `Endpoint.paginate` (or `ControlSiloOrganizationEndpoint.paginate`) implementation/signature, so we cannot verify whether it forwards arbitrary kwargs to `paginator_cls` (or would raise `TypeError`). The finding depends on code not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — organization_context is not defined anywhere in get(), causing a NameError on every request that reaches this code path, and organization_context.member.has_global_access does not match the actual member/role API shape

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py`, but within the shown `get()` implementation there is no definition/import of `organization_context`. Since this reference is newly added and not established in the surrounding added code, it would raise a `NameError` when that line executes (i.e., for any request hitting this endpoint). The additional claim about `member.has_global_access` API shape is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:67 — The optimized_pagination gate silently changes nothing for non-admins, yielding two different paginator implementations/cursor semantics for the same query param depending on caller, breaking clients that rely on consistent cursor behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a gate in `organization_auditlogs.py` where `optimized_pagination=true` only switches to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` if `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`; otherwise it falls back to `DateTimePaginator`. This means the same query param can yield different paginator/cursor behavior depending on caller permissions, and for non-admins the param is silently ignored. That’s a real, diff-grounded API consistency/UX concern, but it’s not clearly a correctness defect by itself since the fallback preserves prior behavior and restricting the optimized paginator to admins may be intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:176–183 — The max(0, offset) clamp added to the shared BasePaginator.get_result changes slicing behavior for all existing endpoints (negative non-prev offsets now silently clamp to page 0 instead of raising), a platform-wide behavior change unrelated to the audit-log feature and untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes shared pagination behavior in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` by introducing `start_offset = max(0, offset)` for the non-`is_prev` case and then slicing `queryset[start_offset:stop]` instead of `queryset[offset:stop]`. This means a negative `offset` (previously passed through to slicing, which would typically error for Django QuerySets) will now be silently clamped to 0, affecting all endpoints using this paginator. That’s a real, diff-grounded scope/behavior change beyond the audit-log feature, and the diff shows no accompanying tests or safeguards for this new behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] src/sentry/api/paginator.py — No tests added for OptimizedCursorPaginator (negative offsets, prev/next cursor round-trips, enable_advanced_features gating, datetime keys) or for the modified BasePaginator.get_result offset clamping / negative is_prev offset handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new pagination behavior (new OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features flag and negative-offset slicing, plus changed BasePaginator.get_result start_offset/stop computation with special handling when cursor.is_prev). No test changes are shown in the diff, so coverage for these new/changed edge cases (negative offsets, prev/next cursor behavior, gating via enable_advanced_features, and key handling) is absent in this PR, making this a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a generic request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The comment implies negative offsets are a supported performance optimization, but cursor parsing/serialization and all existing paginators assume non-negative offsets; the comment documents a contract change that nothing else honors

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce code paths that explicitly allow/use negative offsets: `DateTimePaginator.get_result` now uses `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which permits negative `offset` when `cursor.is_prev` is true, and the newly added `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly slices with `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`. So the comment in `Cursor.__init__` is not documenting a contract change that “nothing else honors” within this diff; at least these paginator paths do honor it. Claims about cursor parsing/serialization assumptions are not verifiable from the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:890–899 — The is_prev trimming logic uses the raw offset while slicing used start_offset; when they differ (negative offset path), the trim condition computes against a length that can't match, producing off-by-one/duplicate rows on prev-page navigation

adjudication.rationale: In both updated paginator implementations, the `is_prev` trimming logic only runs inside `if cursor.is_prev and cursor.value:`. In that code path, slicing uses `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so when `cursor.is_prev` is true, `start_offset` is set to `offset` (the “raw offset”) and they do not differ. Likewise, in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`’s negative-offset branch, `start_offset = cursor.offset` and `offset = cursor.offset`, so they also match. Therefore the claimed mismatch between `start_offset` and `offset` for `is_prev` trimming is not supported by the diff.
